evidence: The density and thickness of the layers are conventionally determined using X-ray reflectometry (XRR). Densities can be determined for layers down to 0.5 nm with a high precision. Another methodology for the density determination is to use a combination of techniques for coverage analysis and thickness measurements. The combination of Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS) with transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has been applied for the density determination of HfO2 layers. Impurities in layers are conventionally investigated using dynamic SIMS. TXRF is a well-established technique for the metallic contamination analysis of semiconductor substrates. Grazing incidence –XRF (GI-XRF) has in addition capabilities for the characterization of thin layers. The methodology consists of measuring the fluorescent intensities as a function of the incident angle and an iterative fitting procedure to obtain the best fit of the calculation on the experimental data. The results are compared with RBS results measured on the same series of samples. TOF-SIMS depth profiles were obtained using a commercial instrument (Iontof-IV).
